tasks.title: Refactor 2 xfail health-check tests to deterministic async-mocks
tasks.description:
Originally tracked as TaskMaster #19 follow-up (closed 2026-08-04) and re-surfaced in this session's commits d93a98a + c6af5d8 (both reverted in 906d1ae due to Linux CI flake). The 2 tests are: test_get_health_status_unhealthy_when_vector_store_unhealthy and test_get_health_status_marks_slow_dependency_degraded, in apps/api/tests/unit/api/test_health.py.

Goal: replace the @pytest.mark.xfail(strict=False) decorators with deterministic async-mocks so backend-tests (unit) is green on Linux CI (Python 3.12 + pytest-asyncio Mode.AUTO + pytest-xdist).

Local pytest (Windows + Python 3.14) shows the refactor works (13/13 pass on both d93a98a and c6af5d8 versions). On CI Linux, both tests fail with result.status == HEALTHY instead of UNHEALTHY/DEGRADED, meaning the monkeypatch.setattr on api.health.get_vector_store did not take effect — production code still calls chromadb init which returns a real ChromaPropertyStore on Linux (vs None on Windows where FastEmbed is unavailable).

Failed fix attempts in this session:
1. d93a98a: @functools.lru_cache()-wrapped _no_vector_store() — failed on CI.
2. c6af5d8: plain def _no_vector_store() (no lru_cache) + per-call asyncio.Event() inside _slow_vector — failed on CI.

Hypotheses to investigate:
- pytest-asyncio Mode.AUTO loop scoping under xdist workers on Linux
- monkeypatch.setattr with string target vs module reference
- asyncio.to_thread behavior with async functions on Linux vs Windows
- Whether the autouse clear_lru_caches fixture interferes with monkeypatched values
- Whether a module-level patch on api.dependencies vs api.health matters

Acceptance criteria:
- pytest tests/unit/api/test_health.py passes 13/13 locally
- pytest on Linux Python 3.12 + pytest-asyncio Mode.AUTO + xdist passes 13/13
- backend-tests (unit) GitHub Actions job on the test commit is completed/success
- @pytest.mark.xfail decorator removed on both tests
tasks.details:
STATE 2026-11-07 — the deterministic refactor LANDED (this task moves from `deferred` to `in-progress`; the last two acceptance criteria are gated on the operator's push).

WHAT LANDED
- The `@pytest.mark.xfail` decorators are REMOVED from both tests (test_get_health_status_unhealthy_when_vector_store_unhealthy and test_get_health_status_marks_slow_dependency_degraded). They are ordinary, enforcing tests on every platform now — an xfail that can never fail documents nothing.
- The root cause was the patching seam, not the code under test. The dependency checks were patched through a dotted import path ("api.health.check_vector_store"), and the patcher resolves such a path by IMPORTING the module by name — which can land on a different module object than the one the function under test reads its globals from. The patch then has no effect, the real check runs, and the test fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. The checks are now patched on the module object directly.
- The Linux symptom was a messenger, not the cause: on the CI image chromadb IS installed, so the real check succeeded and reported healthy, while on a machine without it the same test passed for the WRONG reason (the check reported "not initialized" and therefore unhealthy). Replacing the check itself makes the outcome identical everywhere.
- The slow-dependency test's sleep now outlasts both the handler's internal 4s budget and the test's outer wait, so the outcome cannot depend on which timer a loaded event loop happens to process first.
- A new test, test_the_patch_seam_holds, pins the property the two tests depend on: the module the test patches must be the module the function under test reads its globals from. If that ever breaks again, the failure is one precise assertion instead of a mystery.
- A mutation check confirmed the enforced test is load-bearing: with the patch neutralised it fails with exactly the CI symptom (healthy != unhealthy). The local file is 15/15 green.

WHAT REMAINS (one push, one CI run)
- "pytest on Linux Python 3.12 + pytest-asyncio Mode.AUTO + xdist passes" and "the backend-tests (unit) GitHub Actions job on the test commit is completed/success" both need the commit to reach GitHub, and the push needs the operator's explicit word (project Rule 1). Nothing else is outstanding.

NOTE FOR THE PUSH

tasks.title: [solo] P0 — The vector store's coordinates never reach the property schema (lat/lon vs latitude/longitude)
tasks.description: Every property in the demo loses its coordinates, so the map, the City Overview and the geo filters are all dead. Measured on the live deployment (realty.kittray.com, image 5.1.9) on 2026-11-07: the ChromaDB collection "properties" holds 250 documents whose metadata keys are "lat" and "lon" (read straight from the collection on the node), while the API's property schema and the frontend's extractMapPoints read "latitude" and "longitude". The search response therefore carries latitude: null, longitude: null for every listing. The visible consequences: the City Overview page renders "$0 avg, $0 - $0" for every city (Krakow, Katowice, Lublin, ...), because extractMapPoints drops every point whose latitude/longitude is not a number and the price average is computed from the empty list, and the map itself has no markers. The radius and polygon filters cannot work either. apps/web/src/components/search/property-map-utils.ts:19-46 reads prop.latitude/prop.longitude; apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:42-45 declares SearchResultItem as { property: Property; score: number }.
tasks.details: Find the boundary where the divergence happens and normalize it once, in ONE place, so both spellings are accepted on read and one is written. The loader (apps/api/data/csv_loader.py) fills latitude/longitude on the data frame and the vector-store writer stores them under lat/lon; the property schema (apps/api/db/models.py, apps/api/db/schemas.py) and the API's serialiser expect latitude/longitude. Decide the canonical key (the schema's latitude/longitude), write that in the metadata, and make the reader tolerate the old lat/lon so an existing collection keeps working. Then check the rest of the chain that consumes coordinates: the map's markers and the price heatmap (apps/web/src/components/search/property-map.tsx), the city overview (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/city-overview/page.tsx), the radius filter and the polygon geo-draw. The demo data must be re-seeded after the change (see the seed task) - the deployed collection keeps the old keys until then.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: a test that seeds one property into the vector store and asserts the search response carries non-null latitude/longitude (and that a record written under the legacy lat/lon keys still reads back). Frontend: a unit test for extractMapPoints over a SearchResultItem whose property has coordinates, asserting one point with the right lat/lon and price_per_sqm. Live: on the deployment, /en/city-overview shows a non-zero average price per city and the map renders markers.

tasks.title: [solo] P1 — The sign-in page offers Google and Apple, but the deployment has no OAuth
tasks.description: The sign-in page offers Google and Apple, and the deployment has neither. A visitor who clicks Google gets a 403 and a toast that shows the raw API string "Google OAuth is not enabled" (apps/api/api/routers/auth_jwt.py:847; the Apple branch at :1082 says "Apple Sign-In is not enabled"). Measured on the live demo on 2026-11-07 with a Playwright click: the console shows "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 403 ()" for GET /api/v1/auth/oauth/google and GET /api/v1/auth/oauth/apple, and the backend log carries the matching HTTPException. The buttons are rendered unconditionally by apps/web/src/components/auth/OAuthButtons.tsx (no capability check), and the error text reaches the visitor verbatim because the frontend passes the API detail straight into toast.error. The demo also has JWT auth disabled, so the only working path is "Try without an account".
tasks.details: Decide the contract first: a provider button appears only when the backend says that provider is configured. The cleanest shape is a capability endpoint the sign-in page reads (which providers are enabled), or an existing provider-status call reused - the backend already knows the answer at apps/api/api/routers/auth_jwt.py:847 and :1082, so the UI should not have to guess. Then: render the Google/Apple buttons only for enabled providers, and when a provider call fails, show a human sentence instead of the API detail (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:308 throws the backend detail; apps/web/src/components/auth/OAuthButtons.tsx:25 puts it into a toast). For the public demo the expected result is a sign-in page with "Try without an account" and no OAuth buttons. If OAuth should really be enabled on the deployment instead, that is a separate decision about a client id, a callback URI and a secret - do not smuggle it into this task.
tasks.testStrategy: Frontend: a test that renders the sign-in page with the capability response saying OAuth is disabled and asserts that no Google/Apple button is rendered, plus one that asserts the buttons appear when a provider is enabled. A test that a failed provider call produces a friendly message and not the raw API detail. Live: clicking through the demo's sign-in page produces no 403 in the console and no OAuth button.

tasks.title: [solo] P1 — The demo catalogue has no titles, no addresses and incoherent numbers
tasks.description: The catalogue is 250 rows of random numbers, and the interface shows it. Measured on the live deployment on 2026-11-07: a search for Krakow returns cards titled "Untitled Property" (the title field is null), and the stored document reads "Property in Poznan. Loft with 3 rooms and 1 bathrooms. Listing: Sale, Price: 464576 PLN, area: 192.0 square meters, floor 9 of 8. Amenities: elevator." - a floor above the building's total floors, a 192 m2 loft with one bathroom, and no address, no title, no description. The metadata of the 250 collection documents carries only: area_sqm, bathrooms, city, currency, district, has_elevator, has_garage, has_garden, has_parking, has_pool, id, lat, listing_type, lon, price, price_per_sqm, property_type, rooms, source_url, year_built. The hand-written demo listings in apps/api/alembic/seed.py:30-130 do have titles, addresses and descriptions, but they never reach the vector store, so the demo shows the CSV's noise instead. A visitor sees a catalogue of 250 identical-looking, untitled, incoherent listings - which is exactly what makes the demo look unfinished.
tasks.details: Make the demo catalogue read like a real market. Two sources exist and they disagree: the 25 hand-written listings in apps/api/alembic/seed.py (rich: title, address, description, PLN price, district) and the CSV-loaded rows the demo actually serves (numeric noise). Pick the demo's catalogue deliberately: either seed the hand-written listings into the vector store as well, or generate coherent rows from the CSV's cities (a per-city price band, a floor below the total floors, a room count that matches the area and the type, a street address, a title and a description). Then make the numbers agree with each other: floor <= total_floors, bathrooms consistent with rooms, price consistent with area and city, price_per_sqm recomputed rather than inherited. The generator that builds the document text and the metadata lives in apps/api/data/csv_loader.py and apps/api/alembic/demo_data_generator.py - fix it at the source and re-seed, rather than patching the displayed strings.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: a test over the generated catalogue asserting the invariants - every listing has a title, an address, a description, coordinates, and floor <= total_floors; price_per_sqm equals price / area_sqm; no null title in the search response. Live: the demo's search results show real titles and addresses, and no card reads "Untitled Property".

tasks.title: [solo] P1 — The interface prices zloty in dollars
tasks.description: The interface quotes zloty as dollars. The API returns currency "PLN" and prices in zloty (a Krakow rent of 276040.0 PLN), but the UI prints a dollar sign unconditionally: apps/web/src/components/search/property-map.tsx:118 renders `$${p.price.toLocaleString()}`, and the price filter control offers "Under $300k", "$300k-$600k", "$600k-$1M" (apps/web/src/components/search/map-controls.tsx:258-274). The property already carries `currency` (PLN in the demo, and the API's schema has the field); render it next to every price - the cards, the map markers, the city overview averages and the price filter bands. Decide the display convention once (symbol per currency, a thousands separator per locale) and use it everywhere, so a card, a map popup and a filter agree. The demo's market is Polish, so PLN is the default; a visitor with a different locale should still see the currency they are paying in, not a converted number. The price filter bands (map-controls.tsx) must be derived from the same currency the prices carry.

tasks.title: [solo] P1 — Five tools build their own LLM and die on the demo's missing Zhipu key
tasks.description: Five features of the demo are dead because the tools build their own LLM instead of using the one the app resolved. The live backend logs, on every start: "Failed to create LLM for description generator: Zhipu AI API key required", the same for the headline generator, the social media generator, the price forecast and the neighborhood summary. The cause is in apps/api/tools/price_forecast_tools.py:154-166: when no LLM is injected, the tool calls ModelProviderFactory.create_model(provider_name=settings.default_provider) directly, so it bypasses both the demo's MockLLM ("Demo mode active - using MockLLM (no real API calls)") and the per-user/per-task preference cascade that the rest of the application uses (apps/api/api/dependencies.py, get_llm_for_task). The demo's default provider is zai and there is no key, so the tool's LLM is None and the feature silently degrades. The same pattern is in tools/listing_generator_tools.py (three tools) and tools/neighborhood_summary.py.
tasks.details: Resolve the LLM the way the rest of the application does, in one place. The dependency injector already knows the cascade: request parameter -> task-specific preference -> global preference -> settings default -> Ollama fallback, and the demo mode's MockLLM. The tools should receive that LLM instead of constructing one; where a tool is created outside the request path, it should ask the same factory for the resolved model rather than reading settings.default_provider directly. Then decide what each tool does when no LLM can be built at all - the honest answer is a clear message ("this feature needs an LLM provider"), not a warning in a log the visitor never sees. Check the other tools in apps/api/tools/ for the same construction pattern - this one is the visible symptom, not necessarily the only place.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: a test that builds each of the five tools with no LLM injected while the demo mode is active, and asserts that the resolved LLM is the MockLLM and not None; a test that a tool with no available provider returns a clear error rather than a silent empty result. Live: the backend log carries no "Failed to create LLM" line after a restart, and the price forecast / neighborhood summary / listing generator features answer in the demo.

tasks.title: [solo] P2 — The startup seed is not idempotent and aborts on every boot after the first
tasks.description: The demo's seed is not idempotent, so every boot fails part-way and the failure is swallowed. The live backend logs on each start: "Auto-seed failed (non-fatal): (sqlite3.IntegrityError) UNIQUE constraint failed: notification_preferences.user_id [SQL: INSERT INTO notification_preferences (id, user_id, ...)]" - the seed inserts fixed rows (user-seed-001, user-seed-002) on every start, and the second start collides. The exception is caught and logged as a warning in apps/api/api/main.py:284-292, so the seed aborts at that point and the rest of the seed never runs. That is how the deployment ends up with a catalogue that was seeded once and never again, and with a fresh database that would come up half-seeded - the failure mode this same block was written to prevent (the comment above it records the 2026-11-06 incident where an empty catalogue was the result).
tasks.details: Make the seed safe to run twice. Every insert should be an upsert or a skip-if-exists, keyed by the natural key (the user's id for notification_preferences, the property id for catalogue rows, the agent id for agents). The seed is meant to run on every start of a demo deployment (SEED_ON_STARTUP=true), so "already there" is the normal case, not an error. Second, stop swallowing the failure: apps/api/api/main.py logs it as a warning and continues, which is what turned a hard error into a half-seeded deployment - log the failure with the seed step that failed and make the outcome visible (a health field or a startup summary that says what was seeded). Third, decide whether a restart should re-seed the catalogue at all, or only fill what is missing - the demo's data is meant to be stable, so "fill what is missing" is the safer semantic.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: a test that runs the seed twice against a fresh in-memory database and asserts the second run succeeds, that the row counts are unchanged, and that no unique-constraint error is raised. A test that asserts the startup path reports a seed failure loudly when the seed does fail. Live: the backend log after a restart carries no "Auto-seed failed" line.

tasks.title: [solo] P2 — The newsletter box appears on every page and silently delivers nothing
tasks.description: The demo asks for e-mail addresses and throws them away. Every page of the live deployment carries a newsletter box - "Get new listings in your inbox / Leave your email and we will send you the properties that match your search. / By subscribing you agree to receive property updates by e-mail. You can unsubscribe at any time." - while the backend logs "No email configuration found in environment. Using dummy service (emails will not be sent)." The form accepts an address, promises a subscription and delivers nothing; on a page the visitor may read as a real product, that is the worst kind of broken. The same service drives the account e-mails (verification, password reset), so on the demo those are equally dead - which is a fact the interface does not admit.
tasks.details: Make the deployment say what it is. Two halves: (1) the demo's frontend must not promise what the deployment cannot do - hide the newsletter box when the mail service is a dummy, or state plainly that the demo does not send e-mail; the capability has to reach the frontend (the same shape as the OAuth capability in the sign-in task). (2) the backend must not fail silently where the feature is genuinely expected: the dummy email service should log at warning level with the reason and expose its state (a health field, a settings flag) so the operator can see that mail is off. Decide separately what the demo does with the account e-mails - a visitor who signs in with "Try without an account" gets nothing, and if sign-in is on, the verification mail has to go somewhere real or the path has to be visibly disabled.
tasks.testStrategy: Frontend: a test that renders the newsletter box with the mail capability off and asserts it is not rendered (or renders the "the demo does not send e-mail" wording), and one that asserts it is rendered when mail is configured. Backend: a test that the health payload reports the mail service state. Live: the demo's pages carry no newsletter box that promises delivery.

tasks.title: [solo] P3 — Two deprecations the CI never sees: FastAPI's regex parameter and LangChain's buffer memory
tasks.description: Two deprecation warnings fire on every backend start, and neither the CI nor the lint catches them. The live log carries: "apps/api/api/routers/agent_analytics.py:161: FastAPIDeprecationWarning: `regex` has been deprecated, please use `pattern` instead" (and the same at :267), and "apps/api/ai/memory.py:145: LangChainDeprecationWarning: The class `ConversationBufferMemory` was deprecated in LangChain 0.3.1 and will be removed in 2.0.0. Use `langchain.agents.create_agent` instead". The first is a one-line API change. The second is a removal scheduled for LangChain 2.0: the buffer memory is on the conversation path, so the next major upgrade of the dependency breaks the chat's memory. Both warnings are printed to stdout and then scroll away - nobody reads them.
tasks.details: Fix the FastAPI one in place: `regex` becomes `pattern` in the two query-parameter declarations in apps/api/api/routers/agent_analytics.py, and the behaviour is unchanged (the pattern string is the same). The LangChain one needs a decision rather than a rename: ConversationBufferMemory is deprecated in favour of langchain.agents.create_agent with a checkpointer or the Store API for long-term memory. Read how the memory is used in apps/api/ai/memory.py before changing it - the replacement has to keep the same conversation semantics (what the agent remembers between turns, how long it keeps it), because a silent change of the memory semantics is worse than the warning. Consider turning the deprecation warnings into a CI failure (a warnings filter or a pytest -W error for the project's own modules) so the next one does not arrive unnoticed.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: the existing agent_analytics route tests still pass after the parameter rename; a test for the chat's memory path asserting that a second turn sees the first turn's context after the migration. CI: the backend job runs with the project's own deprecation warnings promoted to errors. Live: the backend log after a restart carries no FastAPIDeprecationWarning and no LangChainDeprecationWarning.

tasks.title: [solo] P3 — The deployment has no error tracking, while the CSP already allows Sentry
tasks.description: The deployment has no error tracking, and it says so only in a log line nobody reads. The live backend logs on every start: "sentry-sdk not installed - error tracking disabled" (apps/api/api/sentry_init.py). The frontend's Content Security Policy, meanwhile, explicitly allows Sentry's origins - sentry.io and *.ingest.sentry.io (apps/web/next.config.ts) - so the browser side is prepared for an error tracker that is not there. The consequence on a public deployment: when a page throws, the stack trace exists only in the container's stdout, where it is lost on the next restart and is invisible to the operator. This is the same class of defect as the ones the visitor sees - invisible failure - but on the operator's side.
tasks.details: Decide the direction, then make it true. Either (a) install sentry-sdk in the backend image (deploy/docker/Dockerfile.backend) and wire a DSN through the deployment's environment, with the release gated on it, or (b) accept that the project does not use Sentry and remove the dead CSP entries so the policy states what is actually allowed. If (a), the DSN is a credential: it belongs in the deployment's environment and nowhere else, and the release must not depend on a key that may be absent - the SDK has to stay quiet when no DSN is configured. If (b), also check the frontend for a sentry client that is never initialised. While in the code, make the "no error tracking" state visible where the operator looks - the health payload - instead of a startup log line.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: a test that the health payload reports the error-tracking state; a test that the SDK initialises without a DSN without raising. Frontend: a test asserting the CSP matches the trackers the app actually loads. Live: the deployment's health endpoint says whether error tracking is on, and the log no longer claims a capability the image does not have.

tasks.title: [solo] P2 — Two schema validators silently drop whole listings from the search results
tasks.description: The Property schema rejects two ordinary listing shapes, and the search router catches the error and skips the row, so the listing vanishes from the results with only a log line to show for it. Verified on 2026-11-07 against apps/api/data/schemas.py: a listing priced below 50 fails the price validator ('Price suspiciously low (<50)', schemas.py:171-177) and a title shorter than 5 characters fails the title field ('String should have at least 5 characters', schemas.py:58); in both cases Property.model_validate raises and apps/api/api/routers/search.py:225-230 logs a warning and continues, so the property never reaches the response. The demo's own 250 listings do not trip either rule (the live collection's cheapest is 134000 PLN and no document carries a title key), so the demo looks healthy - but this project is open source and its users load their own listings: a shared room at 45 EUR or a title like 'ABC' disappears without a word to the visitor. The validators were written to catch data errors; here they silently delete valid listings. The same validators run on every other path that builds a Property, so a dropped listing stays dropped everywhere.
tasks.details: Decide what the two validators are for and make them do that job without deleting the listing. The price rule (ge 50) and the title length rule (min_length 5) are sanity checks on data the pipeline produced, not requirements of the domain: a monthly rent below 50 and a short title are both legitimate listings, and the demo's own price range starts in the hundreds of thousands. The likely intent was to catch a parser that produced a price of 0 or None, so scope the rule to that case (reject only a null/NaN/negative price, accept a small positive one) and treat the title length as a display concern rather than a validity one - a short title is rendered as-is, and the card already has a fallback for a missing one ('Untitled Property' in the city overview). Whatever the outcome, the search router must not delete a listing because of it: if a listing cannot be parsed, the response should say so rather than quietly return a shorter list than the catalogue holds. Fix the validators in apps/api/data/schemas.py at the source rather than special-casing the search router, so the favorites, CMA and reranker readers inherit the same behaviour.
tasks.testStrategy: Backend: a test over Property asserting that a listing priced 40 and one titled 'ABC' both validate (and that a null price and a NaN price still do not); a search-router test asserting that a collection holding such a listing returns it rather than dropping it. Live: load a CSV with a cheap listing and a short title and see it in the search results.

The mock in apps/web/__mocks__/next-intl.tsx resolves the real en.json, so a missing key shows up as the key itself instead of silently passing.

Two guards already exist and must survive this work:

  - the locale parity check (apps/web/messages/*.json, nine files, same key set everywhere) is the acceptance criterion for a finished page.

Repo support: 16 providers in apps/api/models/provider_factory.py and per-task preferences - but NO per-user key storage was found (only the global settings.update_api_key, which mutates os.environ). WHAT THE ROUTE IS NOW
Three panes at lg - the filters 248px, the results 460px, the map the rest; at 390 the panes stack and the map pane is reordered with order-* only, so the DOM order stays the desktop order. The parsed chips sit under the query bar, and the count rides in that row as the landing instrument does it. THE THREE NEW COMPONENTS, AND THEIR TESTS

The area card's statistics are computed from the listings the search returned, and the tests cover the degenerate cases: no listings, a listing without a price, without an area, without a year, a single listing, the median of three, and the area with the most listings winning.

THE DECISIONS THE LANE MADE, AND WHY THEY ARE RIGHT
- The area card carries NO trend and NO days-on-market: the API carries neither, and a number the API does not carry is a number nobody can check.
- Its third statistic is the median YEAR built, not the median price: with one listing in the area a median price equals the listing price, and the specs locate the price by text.
- The filters keep the application's own inputs (#min-price, #max-price, #rooms are number inputs; type and sort are selects), because the e2e fills those inputs - the prototype's range slider and segmented room buttons could not be used.
- The price renders exactly once per listing: a rented flat shows no second monthly figure, or the e2e's price regex matches twice and the strict mode breaks.
- Exactly one button on this route may be named like a filter, and it must be hidden at 1440 - the spec clicks getByRole('button', {name: /filters|filter/i}) before the first search. That is why "Clear Filters" became "Reset" and the mobile Filters pill is lg:hidden.
- The map stays a dynamic import and is mounted only once there is something to place on it, so Leaflet never reaches the first paint.

The switch changed meaning: the map is a pane of the route and is open by default, "List" narrows the route to the list and "Map" brings the pane back. The spec's click on a filter-named button is guarded by isVisible(), so the rename does not break it.

The wave's rule is now: en.json and pl.json are mandatory, the other seven are optional and welcome when a lane can translate them. The lane translated all nine and they were kept.

tasks.title: [agents] P1 - Make sign-in real: split DEMO_MODE, fix the token priority, capture consent
tasks.description: Split DEMO_MODE into four independent flags, fix the token priority that ignores a real session, and capture GDPR consent at registration, so a visitor can actually sign in on the public demo.
tasks.details:
THE BLOCKER
apps/api/api/deps/auth.py:216 returns the synthetic demo user BEFORE the token is read, so a signed-in user is ignored and real sign-in is structurally impossible on the current deployment. Fix: extract the token first and fall back to the demo user only when there is no token AND demo_user_bypass is on. With it off, /auth/me returns 401 for an anonymous visitor, AuthContext falls into demo mode and the Gate shows.

THE SPLIT (apps/api/config/settings.py) - four flags, every one defaulting to today's DEMO_MODE so existing deployments are byte-identical until they opt in:
- demo_data_mode (DEMO_DATA_MODE) - catalogue seeding, apps/api/api/main.py:328
- demo_llm_mode (DEMO_LLM_MODE) - the mock LLM, apps/api/api/dependencies.py:296,430,541, apps/api/utils/free_tier.py:152, apps/api/tools/llm_resolution.py:53
- demo_api_key_bypass (DEMO_API_KEY_BYPASS) - the fake API key, apps/api/api/auth.py:45,151
- demo_user_bypass (DEMO_USER_BYPASS) - the synthetic demo user, apps/api/api/deps/auth.py:216
Target for the public demo: DEMO_DATA_MODE=true, DEMO_LLM_MODE=false, DEMO_API_KEY_BYPASS=true, DEMO_USER_BYPASS=false.

SETTINGS ON THE DEPLOYMENT
AUTH_JWT_ENABLED=true (already the compose default), AUTH_REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true, AUTH_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED=false (the operator's decision: e-mail plus password, no forced verification), and a JWT_SECRET_KEY in the server environment - never in the repository. The five auth tables (users, refresh_tokens, oauth_accounts, password_reset_tokens, email_verification_tokens) are already in the initial Alembic migration, so NO migration is needed. AUTH_OAUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED stays off unless a Google client exists; OAuthButtons.tsx is already capability-gated.

GDPR CONSENT
apps/api/db/models.py:68 has gdpr_consent_at but the register handler never sets it. UserCreate gains consent_given; the register handler writes gdpr_consent_at; the register form gets a required checkbox with a privacy link. The column exists, so no migration.

CAPABILITIES
apps/api/api/routers/capabilities.py publishes auth.jwt_enabled, email.enabled, lead_capture.waitlist_enabled and the llm state, so the UI never promises what the deployment cannot do.
tasks.testStrategy: pytest in visible paths: a real token beats the demo user; the consent timestamp is written at registration; the four flags default to the old DEMO_MODE behaviour. Playwright: register, sign in, then a gated route renders its signed-in content; an anonymous visitor gets 401 from /auth/me on the demo.

WHAT LANDS

It exists and is currently wired only to POST /api/v1/chat/free. FREE_TIER_ENABLED=true with the cascade openrouter,google,ollama (config/settings.py:378) becomes the fallback when the primary key fails.
- capabilities publishes the effective provider, model and rate state, so the TopBar pill and the chat strip report the truth instead of a fixed string.
- The copy correction in all nine locales: the landing band "A local model", FAQ question 2 ("Do I need a paid API key?"), the TopBar pill "Demo mode - local model, no keys" and the chat strip all become false the moment a hosted provider answers. What the demo says instead is decided in task 51.

WHY THIS MATTERS
A demo that answers with a canned string is a screenshot; a demo that answers with a live model is a product - and it is the only thing that turns a visitor into a GitHub star, a PropVector AI waitlist signup or a studio inquiry.

THE EIGHT RULES OF THE PROTOTYPE
1. Geist only, and Geist Mono for every number, price, route and argument - no serif, no italic.
2. Weight carries the hierarchy.
3. Annotations, not eyebrows: mono text only when it is data (route, source, count, status).

7. Zinc chrome, one teal accent for the single primary action of a screen, one warm amber for what needs attention, status green and red keep their meaning.

WHAT IS ALREADY MEASURED
The tokens, the palette and the type scale are ported and asserted by a unit test; the landing and the chrome were compared against the prototype when they landed. The application routes have not been compared at all - that is the gap this task closes.
tasks.testStrategy: The report exists with a row per route and no row left above "acceptable deviation" without a named file that closes it. The acceptance is repeated at 1440 and 390, in light and in dark, and the screenshots live next to the report. The analyser runs against `tmp/design/realt2/v2` and its two verdicts are MEASUREMENTS, not defaults: the token comparison must name how many prototype token definitions it actually read (it must not be zero - a zero means the definition regex did not recognise the prototype's forms and the verdict is vacuous), and the palette comparison must state its distance threshold and list every literal outside it. A verdict that cannot fail is not a verdict.

subtasks.title: The gap analyser measures the token and the palette deltas
subtasks.description: The gap analyser now measures the token and the palette deltas instead of assuming them: it reads the prototype's three token forms, and the palette verdict has a threshold with every literal outside it named.
subtasks.details:
STATE 2026-11-09 - DONE, in two commits: `81a337920` (the analyser, runnable from the root) and `3c926f876` (it measures instead of assuming).

WHAT WAS WRONG
The token half was VACUOUS: the definition reader matched only `--name: value`, while the prototypes declare colours as `var(--bg,#ffffff)` inline and as quoted JS objects (`'--bg':'#09090b'`). So `defined_in_artifact` was 0 and "no new tokens" was true by default rather than proven.
The palette half had NO THRESHOLD: `closest_repo_match_available` counted "has a nearest neighbour", which is trivially true. And the line that was supposed to carry the verdict compared every colour with ITSELF - always distance 0 - and nothing read the list.

THE FIX
The reader recognises all three forms (`--name: value`, `var(--name, #value)`, `'--name': '#value'`). The palette verdict has a real threshold, and the sources are relative to the artefact's own root, so a literal is attributed to a file - which is what makes "legacy or v2" answerable from the report alone.

THE MEASURED BASELINE - what the acceptance compares against
- Token definitions read: 13 (was 0).
- Matching a repo token by NAME: 0. The prototype names its roles differently - `--bg`, `--fg`, `--bd`, `--ac`.
- Matching a repo token by COLOUR: 12, every one inside the threshold (distances 0.0-0.328).
- With no counterpart: 1 - `--tilef`, the CSS filter the prototype puts on the map tiles. It is not a colour; the repository applies the same filter in code (components/search/property-map.tsx), not as a token. It has its own bucket and is not palette drift.
- Repo tokens with no counterpart in the artefact: 83 of 112 - the internal scale the prototype never names (`--chart-2`..., `--radius-*`, `--text-*`, `--font-*`, `--info`, `--caution`, `--critical`).
- Palette against tmp/design/realt2/v2 (30 files, 1324 literals, 37 distinct): 31 within, 6 outside the threshold PALETTE_THRESHOLD = 100.0. The threshold sits in an empty gap: the furthest literal inside is at 73.4, the closest one outside at 967.4.
- Where the six outside come from: ALL SIX are in `v2/support.js`, the shared legacy file that ships inside the v2 folder. No v2 page carries any of them - every `v2/*.html` was checked. Two of them are not palette colours at all (a shadow and a zero-alpha overlay, which the analyser reads as opaque because it drops the alpha); the other four are the previous generation's warm cream palette.

THE CRITERION THE ACCEPTANCE USES
No v2 PAGE carries a literal outside the threshold, and the legacy file's six are NAMED in the report rather than excluded from the measurement. The analyser measures and names; it does not hide.

WHAT THE ANALYSER DOES NOT PROVE
The component list ("not in the repo": ReMap, classList, divIcon, getItem, initMap, isChart, isTable, layerGroup, onSelect, removeItem, setItem) is the prototype's own Leaflet wrapper and JavaScript built-ins. The copy check's "missing keys" (`seo.structuredData`, `tools.map`) are NAMESPACES in the catalogue, not leaves - a false positive of the namespace.leaf heuristic. No real key is missing.

THE COMMAND
`python scripts/design/design_gap.py tmp/design/realt2/v2` - the v2 folder, not the whole tree: the whole tree still holds the previous generation next to it (38 files), which adds ten more literals outside the threshold from Landing.dc.html, Landing Mobile.dc.html, Redesign Story.dc.html, Search.dc.html and the root copy of support.js.

THE FIRST CUT WAS REJECTED, AND WHY
The first capture of the third scene caught an HTTP 429 - the free tier answers with "Hourly limit exceeded" on the twentieth anonymous request of an address (20/h + 200/day per IP, apps/api/utils/free_tier.py, sliding window). The capture ran from the same address whose hourly budget the limiter verification had just spent, so the clip showed the error message instead of an answer. A published clip must never carry a 429, and the capture must therefore be a first-class step with its own checks rather than a side effect of "take a screenshot".

THE SAME CAPTURE ALSO TAUGHT A LESSON WORTH KEEPING
The onboarding tour popup appeared in a frame even though the capture set localStorage["onboarding-tour-dismissed-v1"]="1" at document-start. The reason: the init script added the dark class with document.documentElement.classList.add() before that line, and at document-start documentElement is still null - the throw skipped every later statement, including the flag. Every statement in an init script needs its own guard. The tour shows 1.5 s after mount (apps/web/src/components/onboarding/Tour.tsx) and reads the key in a useEffect.

THE CAPTURE, AS A RECIPE
- Three scenes, all dark, all from the live deployment: the landing, the search with its results, the assistant answering with its citations.
- The theme is the deployment's own (colorScheme dark in the browser context), and the tour is dismissed before the first frame.
- The chat scene is only accepted when the response is HTTP 200 and the pane shows an answer with sources - a 429 is a failed capture, not a scene.
- The capture runs when the address has budget left, or from a signed-in session, or against a local stack that answers with the real provider.

THE ELEMENT ON THE LANDING
- A poster frame with one teal play button (the design system's one primary action per screen), the clip muted and looping, autoplay off, and a caption that names the routes in mono: /en/search, /en/chat.
- With prefers-reduced-motion the poster is the whole thing and the clip never loads.
- The video is not in the initial chunk: it loads on the click, so the Lighthouse budget on /en (performance 0.90, LCP 2.0 s, CLS 0.001, TBT 10 ms as measured 2026-11-09) stays green.
- The asset home: apps/web/public/clips/demo-6s.mp4 and its poster PNG, under 1.5 MB and under 200 KB.

THE CLIP IS A BUILD-TIME ASSET
The landing plays a file; it does not call the model. Nothing on the landing spends the operator's key, and the free-tier limiter is not touched by the page.

THE REFRESH
The clip shows the application's screens, and the reskin waves (#54, #57, #58) change them. The capture is one command, so the refresh after the reskin is cheap - and the task is not done while the mounted clip shows a screen that no longer exists.
tasks.testStrategy: The landing renders the poster and one play button; clicking plays the clip; with prefers-reduced-motion the clip never autoplays and the poster is shown alone. The Lighthouse budget on /en stays green and the video is not in the initial chunk. The clip carries no HTTP 429 and no rate-limit text - checked by reading the frames. The asset sizes are within the stated limits. The clip is re-cut after the reskin waves, and the mounted asset matches the deployment of the day.

tasks.title: [solo] P1 - The chat renders the model's markdown instead of showing it as characters
tasks.description: The demo now answers with a real model, and the model's markdown reaches the visitor as plain text: the chat shows a literal ### and **. The message body has the prose class but the application ships no markdown renderer and no typography plugin, so the class is inert.
tasks.details:
STATE 2026-11-09 - FOUND WITH LIVE EVIDENCE, not from reading. The six-second clip was captured from the deployed demo on 2026-11-09 and the poster frame (assets/clips/poster.png) shows the answer exactly as a visitor sees it:

    ### Matching apartment in Kraków - **Address:** ul. Kanonicka 21, Kazimierz, Kraków - **Price:** **432,000 PLN** ...

The heading marker and the bold markers are visible as characters. The answer is correct - MiniMax, five citations, the right flat - but it is dressed as raw markdown.

WHY IT IS NEW
The demo answered with a canned MockLLM until v5.1.19, and the mock answered in plain prose, so the raw text looked fine. The switch to the real provider is what exposed it: a hosted model writes markdown by default, and nothing between the model and the pane converts it.

WHAT IS IN THE CODE
- apps/web/src/app/[locale]/chat/page.tsx renders the assistant body as {message.content} inside a div with the class "prose break-words dark:prose-invert text-sm leading-relaxed".
- Neither react-markdown nor remark-gfm nor @tailwindcss/typography is in apps/web/package.json, and the typography plugin is not registered in globals.css. The prose class is therefore INERT: even rendered markdown would come out unstyled.
- There is no markdown renderer anywhere in apps/web/src.

THE FIX, AND THE DESIGN QUESTION IN IT
The renderer is the easy half. The hard half is what a markdown heading is allowed to look like in this design system: the rules say Geist only (no serif, no italic), mono for data rather than for prose, ledgers rather than cards, one teal action per screen. A stock typography plugin brings its own scale, its own colour and its own headings, which is exactly the drift the token port removed. The answer needs to be authored, not inherited:
- Which markdown the model is allowed to produce. The house style is a ledger with a heading and rows; if the answer is a ledger, the renderer and the prompt should agree on that, and the prompt (agents/intent_prompts.py) is where it is settled.
- How a heading, a bold run and a list look in the zinc chrome, at the type scale of apps/web/src/app/globals.css.
- That the answer keeps its citations block and its "generated by AI" note intact.

THE SAFETY LINE
The renderer must not execute raw HTML from the model. react-markdown does not by default - that property has to be kept, and a test has to assert that a model answer carrying a script tag is rendered as text.

THE WAVE RELATION
#54 reskins the chat route - the ToolCard with its mono arguments, the 420px context pane, the toolbelt. This task is not part of that wave and does not wait for it: the defect is on the public demo today. But the renderer it lands must be the one the reskinned chat uses, so it is built as a component (a MarkdownMessage) and not as a change inside the page.

WHAT ELSE THE ANSWER NEEDS
The error path is the same path: apps/web/src/app/[locale]/chat/page.tsx substitutes t('errors.apology', { error: message }) into the body, so an error message goes through the same renderer - it must not be rendered as markdown and must not be able to carry markup.
tasks.testStrategy: A jest test renders a model answer that carries headings, bold, a list and a link, and asserts the rendered output has the elements and not the markers. A second test feeds an answer carrying a script tag and asserts it is rendered as text and no script element reaches the DOM. A third asserts the error path (errors.apology) is rendered as plain text. The chat route in Playwright shows a heading as a heading. The rendered answer is checked against the design system - Geist, the type scale of globals.css, no serif, no italic - and against the house style in docs/marketing/materials.md.

tasks.title: [agents] P2 - The chat stream emits structured tool calls instead of stringified agent steps
tasks.description: The chat's tool cards are parsed from stringified (AgentAction, observation) pairs because the stream sends no structured tool calls. The backend should emit name, arguments and result per call, and the frontend parser becomes a fallback instead of the only path.
tasks.details:
STATE 2026-11-09 - FOUND DURING THE RESKIN WAVE, with live evidence from the chat lane (commit 7b82e04f2). It is the one place the chat bends to the backend.

WHAT HAPPENS TODAY
The chat shows a ToolCard per tool call, with the mono arguments, the result, the intermediate steps and the sources. To draw it, the frontend has to reconstruct the call from the stream's intermediate steps: the backend sends the (AgentAction, observation) pairs STRINGIFIED, and components/chat/tool-calls.ts parses that repr - it also handles the web agent's dicts. It works, but it is a parser standing in for a contract.

The frontend already asks for it: it now always sends include_intermediate_steps: true.

WHAT THE CONTRACT SHOULD BE
Each tool call emits, as data: the tool name, the arguments it was called with, the result it returned, and the sources it read. The frontend then renders the card from the fields and stops guessing. The parser stays as a fallback for the paths that do not emit the structured form - it is not deleted, it stops being load-bearing.

WHERE IT LIVES
The stream's meta event already carries sources and, on request, the intermediate steps. The structured calls belong beside them - the same event, not a new one, so the frontend needs one reader and not two.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CHAT
- The console of the tools (the /en/tools route) runs one tool at a time and shows the raw JSON; the chat's cards and the console's output should agree on the shape of a call.
- The toolbelt is eighteen calls. A parser for eighteen shapes is a maintenance surface that grows with every tool; a contract does not.
- The card shows the arguments in mono. Reconstructed arguments are the model's own formatting of them; the arguments are the tool's call signature.

THE CONSTRAINTS
- The backend does not change its public API shape for other clients: the structured calls are additive, inside the existing meta event.
- The toolbelt's calls come from the agent (langchain Classic in this image - the conversational retrieval chain passes question+context, and the classic StuffDocumentsChain declares input_keys=["input"]). Whatever the chain emits, the adapter that produces the structured call is in one place.
- The frontend's parser keeps working until the backend emits the structured form; the switch is by capability, not by date.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS TASK
The chat's visual design is done (TaskMaster #54). This task is the contract under it - it makes the cards exact rather than approximate. It can land after the wave: the frontend works with the parser meanwhile, which is why the cards are honest today and not broken.
tasks.testStrategy: A backend test asserts that a chat request that triggers a tool call produces a structured call in the stream's meta event: the tool name, the arguments, the result and the sources. A test asserts the structured form is absent when no tool was called, and that the intermediate steps still arrive when include_intermediate_steps is true - the old path is not broken by the new one. A frontend test asserts the chat renders the card from the structured call, and that the parser fallback still renders the card when the backend sends only the stringified pairs.

tasks.title: [solo] P3 - The agent response carries a listing count, so the directory can show the design's Listings column
tasks.description: The design's agent directory carries a Listings column, but the agent response has no listing count, so the column was left out rather than invented. The backend already sorts by listings, so it computes the number - it just does not return it.
tasks.details:
STATE 2026-11-09 - FOUND DURING THE RESKIN WAVE (TaskMaster #54, the agent directory commit 9995de48d).

WHAT THE DESIGN ASKS FOR
tmp/design/realt2/v2/Agents.dc.html gives the directory a Listings column. The reskinned directory does not have it: the API's agent response carries no listing count, and the backend's AgentProfileResponse has no such field.

WHY THE COLUMN IS ABSENT
A number the API does not carry is a number nobody can check. The lane that reskinned the directory left the column out rather than inventing it - and rendered the real count on the profile route instead (listings.length from getAgentListings).

WHY IT IS CHEAP
The backend already sorts by listings (`sort_by=listings` is a sort, not a count), so the number is computed on the way out and simply not returned. The change is one field on the response, and the directory renders it in the prototype's column.

WHAT LANDS
- The agent list response carries a listing count per agent.
- The directory renders the prototype's Listings column with that number - and shows a dash, not a zero, where the count is genuinely unknown.
- The catalogue's own currency of a listing stays as it is: the count is a count, and it does not become a price.

THE CONSTRAINT
The demo catalogue is seeded, so the count is honest there. A deployment with an empty catalogue shows zero, which is also honest - what must not happen is a count that is a guess.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS TASK
The reskin of the directory is done (TaskMaster #54) and its acceptance report will name the missing column as a gap until this lands.
tasks.testStrategy: A backend test asserts that the agent list response carries a listing count per agent, and that the count equals the number of that agent's listings in the catalogue. A frontend test asserts the directory renders the count in the Listings column, and a dash where the count is unknown rather than a zero. The existing agent-list and directory tests stay green.
